description: Backend foundation for all Batch 1 features (server/schema.sql + server/index.js). Adds sku and deleted_at columns + stock_movements table (idempotent), extends the product helpers additively, auto-generates SKUs, records stock movements in a transaction on create/update, converts delete to a soft delete, and adds archive/restore/permanent-delete, stock-movement read routes, and a transactional bulk-import endpoint. The frontend feature (FEAT-002) depends entirely on this; implement and verify this first.
steps: In server/schema.sql, append idempotent DDL after the existing products indexes: `ALTER TABLE products ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS sku VARCHAR(64);`, `ALTER TABLE products ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ;`, `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS products_sku_idx ON products(sku) WHERE sku IS NOT NULL;`, `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS products_deleted_at_idx ON products(deleted_at);`. Then add the stock_movements table verbatim: `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS stock_movements ( id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY, product_id BIGINT REFERENCES products(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, user_id BIGINT, user_name VARCHAR(120), delta INTEGER NOT NULL, stock_before INTEGER NOT NULL, stock_after INTEGER NOT NULL, reason VARCHAR(255), created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW() );` and `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS stock_movements_product_idx ON stock_movements(product_id, created_at DESC);`.

In server/index.js, extend the `productFields` string to include `sku` and `deleted_at`. In `normalizeProduct(row)`, add `sku: row.sku ?? null` to the returned object (keep every existing field unchanged so the response shape is only additive). Leave `productValues(body)` returning its current positional columns; handle sku explicitly in the routes so the INSERT/UPDATE column lists stay explicit.

Add a `generateSku()` helper near the other helpers: `return 'SKU-' + Date.now().toString(36).toUpperCase() + '-' + crypto.randomBytes(2).toString('hex').toUpperCase()`. `crypto` is already imported. In the create path, when a generated sku collides (INSERT throws error.code === '23505' on products_sku_idx), retry generation a few times before surfacing the error.

Rewrite `POST /api/products` to use the transaction pattern from the categories PUT route (const client = await pool.connect(); try { BEGIN ... COMMIT } catch { ROLLBACK; next(error) } finally { client.release() }). Resolve sku = (String(body.sku||'').trim() || generateSku()). INSERT the product including sku and RETURNING ${productFields}. Look up acting user name once: `SELECT name FROM users WHERE id=$1` with request.userId. If the created stock > 0, INSERT a stock_movements row (product_id, user_id=request.userId, user_name, delta=stock, stock_before=0, stock_after=stock, reason = String(body.reason||'').trim() || 'Initial stock'). Respond 201 with normalizeProduct(row). All queries parameterized.

Rewrite `PUT /api/products/:id` with the same transaction pattern. First `SELECT stock, sku FROM products WHERE id=$1 AND deleted_at IS NULL FOR UPDATE`; 404 if no row. Compute new stock from productValues; resolve sku = provided-trimmed-or-keep-existing. UPDATE the product (name, category, price, stock, status, media_*, sku, updated_at=NOW()) RETURNING ${productFields}. If new stock !== old stock, INSERT a stock_movements row (delta = newStock-oldStock, stock_before=oldStock, stock_after=newStock, user_id/user_name as above, reason = body.reason-or 'Manual update'). COMMIT; respond normalizeProduct(row).

Change `GET /api/products` query to `SELECT ${productFields} FROM products WHERE deleted_at IS NULL ORDER BY created_at DESC` so soft-deleted rows are excluded. Change `DELETE /api/products/:id` to a soft delete: `UPDATE products SET deleted_at=NOW(), updated_at=NOW() WHERE id=$1 AND deleted_at IS NULL` returning 404 when rowCount is 0, else 204.

Add `GET /api/products/archived` (requireAuth): `SELECT ${productFields} FROM products WHERE deleted_at IS NOT NULL ORDER BY deleted_at DESC` -> rows.map(normalizeProduct). Add `POST /api/products/:id/restore` (requireAuth): `UPDATE products SET deleted_at=NULL, updated_at=NOW() WHERE id=$1 AND deleted_at IS NOT NULL RETURNING ${productFields}` (404 if none) -> normalizeProduct. Add `DELETE /api/products/:id/permanent` (requireAuth, requireAdmin): `DELETE FROM products WHERE id=$1` (404 if none, else 204).

Add `GET /api/products/:id/movements` (requireAuth): `SELECT id, product_id, user_id, user_name, delta, stock_before, stock_after, reason, created_at FROM stock_movements WHERE product_id=$1 ORDER BY created_at DESC`, mapped to camelCase (id:Number, productId, userId, userName, delta, stockBefore, stockAfter, reason, createdAt). Add `GET /api/stock-movements` (requireAuth, requireAdmin): `SELECT m.id, m.product_id, m.user_id, m.user_name, m.delta, m.stock_before, m.stock_after, m.reason, m.created_at, p.name AS product_name FROM stock_movements m LEFT JOIN products p ON p.id=m.product_id ORDER BY m.created_at DESC LIMIT 200`, mapped to camelCase including productName.

Add `POST /api/products/bulk` (requireAuth) accepting `{ products: [...] }` (reject non-array / empty with 400). In one transaction: look up acting user name once; for each row resolve sku (provided or generateSku), INSERT the product RETURNING ${productFields}, and when stock>0 INSERT an 'Initial stock' movement. COMMIT and respond `{ created: rows.map(normalizeProduct) }`. On any error ROLLBACK and respond 400 `{ message, index }` identifying the failing row (treat 23505 as a duplicate-SKU message). All parameterized.

Keep route registration grouped and consistent with the existing file: distinct subpaths (/archived, /:id/movements, /:id/restore, /:id/permanent, /bulk) alongside the existing /:id routes. Preserve the single next(error) error-handler flow.
acceptance_criteria: server/schema.sql contains the sku + deleted_at columns, the partial unique sku index, the deleted_at index, and the stock_movements table + index, all using IF NOT EXISTS so existing databases upgrade on next boot.
normalizeProduct returns all previously existing fields plus `sku`; no field was renamed or removed.

POST and PUT /api/products run inside a BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK transaction and write a stock_movements row when stock changes (create with stock>0, or update where stock differs), recording delta, stock_before, stock_after, acting user id+name, and reason.

DELETE /api/products/:id sets deleted_at (soft delete); GET /api/products excludes deleted rows; GET /api/products/archived lists them; POST /api/products/:id/restore clears deleted_at; DELETE /api/products/:id/permanent (admin-only) hard-deletes.
GET /api/products/:id/movements (auth) and GET /api/stock-movements (admin, limit 200, joined product name) return newest-first.
POST /api/products/bulk inserts an array of products in one transaction and rolls back entirely on any failure.
Every new SQL statement is parameterized (no string interpolation of user input).
verification: From c:\Users\Falih\Videos\aplikasi\.worktrees\batch1-inventory\crud run `npm.cmd install` (first time) so node_modules exists.
Run `node --check server/index.js` and confirm it exits 0 (valid ESM syntax).
Run `npm.cmd run lint` and confirm no new errors are reported for server/index.js.
Run `npm.cmd run build` and confirm it still succeeds (server changes must not break the client build).

DB smoke test ONLY IF a real .env with a reachable DATABASE_URL exists (currently only .env.example is present, so this is expected to be SKIPPED — record that in findings rather than failing). If reachable: start the server once, confirm it boots (schema applies cleanly), then stop it.
findings:
Backend foundation implemented in server/schema.sql and server/index.js. FEAT-002 (frontend) can rely on the following.

NEW ROUTES (all under http://localhost:3001/api, all require Bearer auth via authHeaders()):
- GET  /api/products            -> existing route, now EXCLUDES soft-deleted rows (WHERE deleted_at IS NULL). Each product object now additively includes `sku` (string|null). Shape otherwise unchanged: {id,name,category,price,stock,status,media,sku,createdAt,updatedAt}.
- POST /api/products            -> transactional. Body may include optional `sku` (trimmed; auto-generated if empty) and optional `reason`. If created stock>0, records an 'Initial stock' movement. Returns 201 normalizeProduct.
- PUT  /api/products/:id        -> transactional, locks row FOR UPDATE, 404 if missing/soft-deleted. `sku` kept if not provided. If stock changes, records a movement (reason defaults to 'Manual update'). Returns normalizeProduct.
- DELETE /api/products/:id      -> now a SOFT delete (sets deleted_at). 204 on success, 404 if already deleted/missing.
- GET  /api/products/archived  -> (auth) soft-deleted products, newest-deleted first.
- POST /api/products/:id/restore -> (auth) clears deleted_at, returns normalizeProduct, 404 if not archived.
- DELETE /api/products/:id/permanent -> (auth + ADMIN only) hard delete, 204 / 404.
- GET  /api/products/:id/movements -> (auth) movement history for one product, newest first.
- GET  /api/stock-movements    -> (auth + ADMIN only) latest 200 movements across all products, newest first, each including `productName` (string|null, LEFT JOIN).
- POST /api/products/bulk      -> (auth) body { products: [ {name,category,price,stock,status?,media?,sku?,reason?}, ... ] }. One transaction: inserts all, records 'Initial stock' movement for each row with stock>0, rolls back entirely on any failure. Success: 200 { created: [normalizeProduct,...] }. Failure: 400 { message, index } where index is the 0-based failing row (duplicate SKU -> message 'Duplicate SKU in import.'). Reject non-array/empty with 400.

GENERATED SKU FORMAT: 'SKU-' + Date.now().toString(36).toUpperCase() + '-' + 2-random-bytes-hex-uppercase, e.g. 'SKU-LZ3K8A-9F1C'. Enforced unique by partial index products_sku_idx (WHERE sku IS NOT NULL); generation retries up to 5x on 23505 collision.

MOVEMENT JSON SHAPE (camelCase from normalizeMovement): { id:Number, productId:Number|null, userId:Number|null, userName:string|null, delta:int, stockBefore:int, stockAfter:int, reason:string|null, createdAt }. The /api/stock-movements variant adds `productName`.

SCHEMA: products gains sku VARCHAR(64) + deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ (ALTER ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS), partial unique index products_sku_idx, index products_deleted_at_idx; new table stock_movements (+ index stock_movements_product_idx). All idempotent.

VERIFICATION: `npm.cmd install` done (node_modules present). `node --check server/index.js` exit 0. `npm.cmd run lint` (oxlint) reports no errors and no new server/index.js warnings (only 3 pre-existing src/App.jsx set-state-in-effect warnings remain). `npm.cmd run build` (vite build) succeeds. DB smoke test SKIPPED: no real .env with a reachable DATABASE_URL exists (only .env.example present), as expected.
